title: FFT Live Audio from Microphone
description: Real-time frequency spectrum visualization of audio input from computer microphone using FFT analysis.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
FFT
Audio Analysis
Real-time Processing
learningObjectives: Identify the fundamental frequency of a sustained hummed or whistled note as the leftmost peak in the live spectrum
Predict how raising the smoothness slider toward 0.95 averages the spectrum across frames, steadying the display but slowing its response to sudden sounds
Predict how increasing the FFT size sharpens the frequency resolution of each spectral bin while requiring more input samples per analysis frame
Compare the spectra produced by a whistle, a spoken vowel, and a hand clap to distinguish tonal sounds from broadband noise
Explain why the FFT analysis requires microphone permission and only updates while the Start button has recording engaged
